blocks.title: Vectors and Component Form
teacherCues: Draw a vector from (0,0) to (3,2) and another from (1,2) to (4,4). Ask: Are they equivalent? (Yes, same length and direction).
Write the formula for component form: v = ⟨x2−x1, y2−y1⟩.

discoveryHook.scenario: A vector represents both how far and in which direction to go—like an arrow showing a plane's velocity: speed (magnitude) and heading (direction).

explanation: A [[kw:vector]] is a quantity with both magnitude and direction. It is represented by a directed line segment.
The [[kw:component form]] of a vector from P(p1,p2) to Q(q1,q2) is v = ⟨q1−p1, q2−p2⟩.
Two vectors are equal if they have the same components.

examples.title: A – Find component form & magnitude
examples.prompt: Given P(4, -7) and Q(-1, 5), find the vector v = PQ and its magnitude.

examples.title: B – Equivalent vectors
examples.prompt: Show that vector u from (0,0) to (3,2) is equivalent to v from (1,2) to (4,4).
examples.peerPrompt: Tell your partner: Compute components and magnitudes. Why does the same slope matter?
steps: Both have same components, so equal.

examples.title: C – Find components
examples.prompt: Initial point (-2, 3), terminal point (-7, 9). Find vector components.

confusionCorner.title: Direction of subtraction
confusionCorner.body: Always subtract the initial point coordinates from the terminal point coordinates: [[imp:terminal − initial]].

questions.prompt: The component form of a vector from P(p1,p2) to Q(q1,q2) is ⟨q1−p1, q2−___⟩.
hints: Subtract the y-coordinate of P from Q.

questions.prompt: What is the magnitude of vector ⟨3, 4⟩? (Enter a number)
If initial point is (0,0) and terminal point is (v1,v2), the vector is ⟨v1, v2⟩ and its magnitude is √(v1² + v2²). This vector is in ___ position.

blocks.title: Vector Operations
teacherCues: Write u=⟨1,3⟩, v=⟨-2,5⟩. Ask: What is u+v? Add components. What is 2u? Multiply each component.

discoveryHook.scenario: Combining velocities: a plane flying east with wind north. Add the vectors to get resultant velocity.

explanation: [[kw:Vector addition]]: u + v = ⟨u1+v1, u2+v2⟩. Geometrically, place the tail of v at the tip of u; the sum is the diagonal.
[[kw:Scalar multiplication]]: kv = ⟨k v1, k v2⟩. The magnitude is |k| times ||v||; if k < 0, direction reverses.

formulaCard.title: Operations
formulaCard.formula: $$\vec{u}+\vec{v} = \langle u_1+v_1, u_2+v_2 \rangle$$ $$k\vec{v} = \langle k v_1, k v_2 \rangle$$

examples.title: B – Scalar multiplication
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to your partner: Multiply each component by the scalar, then subtract.

confusionCorner.title: Subtraction order
confusionCorner.body: u − v means add the negative of v. So components: u1−v1, u2−v2. Not the reverse.

questions.prompt: Let u = ⟨2,5⟩, v = ⟨-1,3⟩. Find u − v's x-component. (Enter a number)
The magnitude of kv equals |k|·||v||. This means that multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its ___.
hints: It makes it longer or shorter.

blocks.title: Unit Vectors and i, j Form
teacherCues: Write: To get a unit vector in the direction of v, divide v by ||v||.
Introduce i = ⟨1,0⟩, j = ⟨0,1⟩. Then any vector ⟨a,b⟩ = a i + b j.

discoveryHook.scenario: A unit vector is like a compass needle: it points a direction but has length 1. Combining multiples of east (i) and north (j) gives any vector.

explanation: A [[kw:unit vector]] has magnitude 1. In direction of v, $$\vec{u} = \frac{\vec{v}}{\|\vec{v}\|}.$$
Any vector can be written as a linear combination: $$\vec{v} = v_1\,\mathbf{i} + v_2\,\mathbf{j}.$$

formulaCard.title: Unit Vector & i,j Form
notes: v1 = ||v|| cos θ, v2 = ||v|| sin θ (for direction angle θ).

examples.title: A – Find a unit vector
examples.prompt: For v = ⟨-2, 5⟩, find a unit vector u in the same direction.

examples.title: B – Check magnitude
examples.prompt: Verify that the unit vector found has magnitude 1.
examples.peerPrompt: Plug the components into the magnitude formula and simplify. Explain why it works.

examples.title: C – Write in i,j form
examples.prompt: Write the vector ⟨3, -7⟩ using i and j.

confusionCorner.title: Unit vector formula
confusionCorner.body: Don't confuse the unit vector with the original vector. The unit vector is [[imp:1/||v||]] times the original v.

hints: By definition, unit vector has length 1.

questions.prompt: The standard unit vector i is ⟨1,0⟩ and j is ⟨___, 1⟩.
Write the vector ⟨4, -3⟩ as a linear combination of i and j. (Enter '4i-3j')
hints: First component times i, second times j.

blocks.title: Direction Angles
teacherCues: Draw a vector v = ⟨v1, v2⟩. The direction angle θ is the angle it makes with the positive x-axis.
Recall: v1 = ||v|| cos θ, v2 = ||v|| sin θ.

discoveryHook.scenario: A plane's heading is its direction angle from north. The vector components tell you how fast east and north the plane is moving.

explanation: The [[kw:direction angle]] θ of a vector v = ⟨v1, v2⟩ is the angle from the positive x-axis to v, where 0 ≤ θ < 2π.
To find θ, use $$\tan \theta = \frac{v_2}{v_1}$$ and adjust quadrant.

formulaCard.title: Direction Angle
notes: Use arctan and adjust for correct quadrant.

examples.title: A – Find direction angle
examples.prompt: Find the direction angle of v = ⟨-5, 12⟩.
steps: Since x negative, y positive, QII.

examples.title: B – Components from angle
examples.prompt: A vector has magnitude 10 and direction angle 30°. Find its components.
examples.peerPrompt: Explain: Which function gives the x-component? The y-component?

examples.title: C – Quadrant check
examples.prompt: If v1 > 0, v2 < 0, which quadrant is the direction angle?
steps: Positive x, negative y → Quadrant IV.

confusionCorner.title: arctan gives reference
confusionCorner.body: Use arctan to get a reference angle, then place it in the correct quadrant based on signs of v1 and v2.

questions.prompt: The direction angle is measured from the positive ___–axis.
hints: Standard position angle from positive x.

questions.prompt: If a vector has magnitude 5 and direction angle 60°, what is its x-component? (Enter 5cos60 = 2.5 as 2.5)
If v = ⟨0, 5⟩, its direction angle is ___ degrees.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid – Application: Finding Resultant Velocity
teacherCues: Problem: A plane heads east at 200 mph; wind blows north at 30 mph. What is the resultant velocity (magnitude and direction)?
Use vector addition: plane = 200i, wind = 30j, resultant = 200i + 30j.

discoveryHook.scenario: Pilots use vectors to compute their actual path when wind is involved. Adding the wind vector to the plane's velocity yields the true course.

explanation: [[imp:Understand]]: Represent velocities as vectors. Plane: v_p = ⟨200, 0⟩. Wind: v_w = ⟨0, 30⟩.
[[imp:Solve]]: Resultant v_r = v_p + v_w = ⟨200, 30⟩. Magnitude = √(200²+30²) ≈ 202.24 mph. Direction: tan θ = 30/200 → θ ≈ 8.53° north of east.
[[imp:Conclude]]: The plane's actual speed is about 202 mph, heading slightly north of east.

examples.title: A – Understand the setup
examples.prompt: A boat is rowed east at 4 mph across a river with a 3 mph current north. Write the vectors.

examples.title: B – Solve for resultant
examples.prompt: Find the boat's actual velocity (magnitude and direction relative to east).
examples.peerPrompt: Discuss: How to combine? How to find angle?

examples.title: C – Conclude
examples.prompt: If a plane flies at 300 mph east, wind 40 mph north, what is the resultant speed?

confusionCorner.title: Direction reference
confusionCorner.body: Always specify direction relative to a known axis, e.g., 'north of east' or 'east of north'.

questions.prompt: A plane flying east at 200 mph with a 30 mph wind from the south (so north wind) experiences a resultant with a northward component of ___ mph.
What is the magnitude of the resultant vector ⟨200, 30⟩? (Round to nearest whole number)
The direction of the resultant is the angle measured from east toward north. For v = ⟨200, 30⟩, tan θ = 30/200, so θ ≈ ___ degrees.

challengeCorner.prompt: A swimmer can swim at 2 mph in still water, heading directly east across a river with a 1 mph current south. Determine the swimmer's actual velocity (magnitude and direction).
hints: Magnitude = √5 ≈ 2.24, angle = tan⁻¹(1/2) ≈ 26.6° south of east.
challengeCorner.feedbackIfWrong: Resultant velocity is approximately 2.24 mph at 26.6° south of east.
